description:
This image displays two photographs illustrating different types of coastal land cover.
The top photograph shows an elevated view of a sandy beach within a turquoise bay, surrounded by arid, rocky hillsides with minimal vegetation, located in Lanzarote, Canary Islands, Spain. Small buildings are visible on the hills overlooking the beach, which is populated by several individuals. This photograph exemplifies a "Beaches" classification, which includes areas of sand, gravel, shingle, pebbles or cobblestones along the sea.
The bottom photograph presents an extensive landscape of sand dunes, stretching towards the distant sea under a clear sky. The foreground shows areas of sparse, scrubby vegetation, characteristic of partially vegetated dunes or sand plains. This photograph illustrates "Dunes and sand plains" land cover, which can include shifting dunes (white dune) or fixed dunes (grey dunes) with open or closed perennial grasslands. Both images depict features relevant to the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) land cover class "6.2.1 Beaches and dunes".
